sections.heading: Equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces

questions.q: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces: $(6,0)$ N, $(-2,5)$ N, and $\mathbf{F}$. Find $\mathbf{F}$.
questions.answer: For equilibrium, the sum of all forces is zero: $\mathbf{F}=-\left[(6,0)+(-2,5)\right]=-(4,5)=(-4,-5)$ N.

questions.q: A particle of weight $20$ N hangs in equilibrium, supported by two strings making angles of $40^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with the ceiling on either side. Set up the two equilibrium equations (horizontal and vertical) using tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$.
A particle is in equilibrium under three forces: $(3,-4)$ N, $(5,1)$ N, and $\mathbf{F}$. Find $\mathbf{F}$.
questions.answer: For equilibrium, the sum of all forces is zero: $\mathbf{F}=-\left[(3,-4)+(5,1)\right]=-(8,-3)=(-8,3)$ N.

sections.heading: Friction and the coefficient of friction

questions.q: A block of mass $5$ kg rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction $\mu=0.3$. Find the maximum friction force before the block slides, using $F=\mu R$ and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
questions.answer: Normal reaction: $R=mg=5(9.8)=49$ N. Maximum friction: $F=\mu R=0.3(49)=14.7$ N.

questions.q: A block of mass $8$ kg rests on a rough horizontal surface. It is on the point of sliding when a horizontal force of $23.52$ N is applied. Find the coefficient of friction $\mu$, using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
questions.answer: Normal reaction: $R=mg=8(9.8)=78.4$ N. At the point of sliding, $F=\mu R$: $23.52=\mu(78.4)$, so $\mu=\dfrac{23.52}{78.4}=0.3$.

questions.q: A block of mass $10$ kg rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction $\mu=0.4$. Find the maximum friction force before the block slides, using $F=\mu R$ and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$.
questions.answer: Normal reaction: $R=mg=10(9.8)=98$ N. Maximum friction: $F=\mu R=0.4(98)=39.2$ N.

questions.answer: Component perpendicular to the plane: $mg\cos(30^\circ)=8(9.8)(0.8660)\approx67.9$ N.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a crate on a ramp with friction

questions.q: This question has two parts. A crate of mass $10$ kg sits on a ramp inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction $\mu=0.25$ between the crate and the ramp. Use $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$. (a) Find the normal reaction force on the crate. (b) Determine whether the crate remains stationary, by comparing the component of gravity along the ramp with the maximum available friction force.
questions.answer: (a) $R=mg\cos(20^\circ)=10(9.8)(0.9397)\approx92.1$ N. (b) Component of gravity along the ramp: $mg\sin(20^\circ)=10(9.8)(0.3420)\approx33.5$ N. Maximum friction: $F_{max}=\mu R=0.25(92.1)\approx23.0$ N. Since $33.5\text{ N}>23.0\text{ N}$, the gravity component exceeds the maximum available friction, so the crate slides down the ramp.
